title: Keep the quote service's in-flight gauge honest

blocks.text: The quote service protects its pricing backend: while `limit` quotes are in flight it refuses new ones with `BusyException`. Yesterday the backend was down for four minutes. It came back, but the service went on refusing every quote until it was restarted, with nothing running, and the gateway, which retries a quote that failed with an `IOException`, never retried anything that morning.

Finish `lookup(...)` in `src/main/java/practice/QuoteService.java`. It counts the quote in `inFlight` for as long as it runs, answers from the cache when it can, and otherwise asks the backend and caches the price.

When you're done, `inFlight()` goes back down however a quote ends: with a price, from the cache, or with whatever the backend throws, checked or not. And the backend's exception reaches the caller of `quote()` as it was thrown. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: a quote is counted in flight while the backend works on it, returns the backend's price, and is no longer counted afterwards
a second quote for the same SKU comes from the cache without calling the backend
a quote asked for while the limit is in flight is refused with BusyException
quotes that fail with an IOException from the backend are no longer counted in flight
quotes that fail with an unchecked exception from the backend are no longer counted in flight
quotes answered from the cache are no longer counted in flight
the exception the backend throws reaches the caller of quote() unchanged

origin.section: A return in finally Throws Away the Exception and the try's Result

concepts: finally runs on every way out of its try: normal end, return, break, continue and an exception of any type, so cleanup written after the block or in one catch misses paths.
A finally that ends with return (or break, continue or its own throw) discards the try's pending exception or return value.
